# Skill Author

Helps you write **new agent skills** that follow the best-practices documented at
https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/ — without you having to re-read those pages
every time. Pairs with `skill-creator` (which handles eval/iterate/optimize loops
once a draft exists).

## When to use this vs `skill-creator`

| Task | Use |
|---|---|
| "I want to make a new skill for X" | **skill-author** (scaffold + author) |
| "Scaffold the SKILL.md / a reference / a script" | **skill-author** |
| "Lint this skill draft" | **skill-author** |
| "My skill isn't triggering when I want it to" | `skill-creator` (description optimization) |
| "Run test cases against my skill, benchmark it" | `skill-creator` (eval loop) |
| "Compare two versions of my skill" | `skill-creator` (blind comparison) |

If both apply, start here, then hand off to `skill-creator` once the draft is solid.

## Workflow

### 1. Capture intent (1 minute)

Before scaffolding, get four answers — usually just by asking the user:

1. **What does it do?** (one sentence)
2. **When should it trigger?** (specific user phrases / contexts)
3. **What does it output?** (file, command result, plan, prose)
4. **Is the output objectively verifiable?** (decides whether `skill-creator` evals are worth the effort later)

Write these four down before touching files. They become the seeds for the
description, the workflow body, and the future eval set.

### 2. Scaffold

Use `scripts/new-skill.sh` to produce the directory layout:

```bash
bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
# creates: skills/local/<skill-name>/{SKILL.md,references/,scripts/,assets/}
# seeds:   SKILL.md from assets/SKILL.md.template
```

The template's frontmatter has placeholders that lint will reject — this is on
purpose so the agent can't forget to fill them in.

### 3. Author the SKILL.md

Read `references/authoring-patterns.md` before writing the body. The patterns
that matter most:

- **Description must be "pushy"** and include concrete trigger contexts. Naive
  descriptions cause undertriggering — the #1 failure mode of new skills.
- **Gotchas section** — environment-specific facts that defy reasonable
  assumptions. The single highest-value section in most skills.
- **Output templates** — agents pattern-match against concrete structures more
  reliably than they follow prose descriptions of formats.
- **Calibrated specificity** — be prescriptive only where the task is fragile;
  give the agent freedom (and explain *why*) where multiple approaches are valid.
- **Defaults, not menus** — pick one tool/approach and mention alternatives as
  escape hatches.

Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. If you blow past that, move detail into
`references/<topic>.md` and tell the agent **when** to load it ("Read X if Y
happens"), not just that it exists.

### 4. Design any scripts

Before writing a script, read `references/script-design.md`. Skills script
design is meaningfully different from "regular" CLI script design because the
caller is an LLM reading your stderr to decide what to do next. The non-obvious
requirements:

- No interactive prompts, ever (agents run in non-interactive shells)
- `--help` is the primary interface documentation — keep it concise but complete
- Errors must say *what was expected* and *what to try*, not just *what failed*
- Structured stdout (JSON/CSV/TSV), prose diagnostics to stderr — separate them
- `--dry-run` for any destructive operation
- Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx` invocations

For Python helpers, prefer **PEP 723 inline dependencies** + `uv run` over
`requirements.txt` — the script becomes self-contained and the agent doesn't
have to set up an environment first.

### 5. Lint

Run the linter before committing or handing off to `skill-creator`:

```bash
bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
```

It checks three things:

1. **Frontmatter & length** — `name` and `description` exist; description has a
   "use when" trigger phrase; SKILL.md is under 500 lines.
2. **Script hygiene** — every `scripts/*.sh` has a shebang, is executable, and
   responds to `--help` (presence of the flag handler, not necessarily a working
   script).
3. **Reference reachability** — every file in `references/` is mentioned at
   least once from `SKILL.md` (no dead reference docs).

Fix every error. Warnings are advisory but usually worth addressing.

### 6. (Optional) Hand off to skill-creator

Once lint passes and the skill *looks* right, the next questions are
quantitative: does it trigger reliably? does it produce good output? That's
`skill-creator` territory. Tell the user: "skill-author got the structure
right. If you want to validate it works on real prompts, the `skill-creator`
skill runs test cases and benchmarks."

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/new-skill.sh <name>`** — Scaffold `skills/local/<name>/` with
  SKILL.md, references/, scripts/, assets/ from templates.
  - Flags: `--vendor` (use `skills/vendor/<name>/` instead — rare, normally
    vendored skills come via `vendor.yaml`); `--dry-run`; `--force` (overwrite
    existing).
- **`scripts/lint-skill.sh <skill-dir>`** — Run frontmatter, script hygiene,
  and reference reachability checks. Exit non-zero on any error.
  - Flags: `--strict` (treat warnings as errors); `--quiet` (only print failures).

## Bundled assets

Templates that `new-skill.sh` copies and that you can reference manually:

- `assets/SKILL.md.template` — Frontmatter + workflow skeleton with placeholders.
- `assets/reference.md.template` — Reference doc skeleton (TOC + sections).
- `assets/script-bash.template` — Bash 3.2 compatible script with `set -euo pipefail`,
  `--help` / `--dry-run` flag handler, structured-output friendly logging
  (data → stdout, prose → stderr).
- `assets/script-python.template` — Python script with PEP 723 inline-deps
  block, argparse with help/examples, dry-run support.

## Reference files

- `references/authoring-patterns.md` — The agentskills.io "best practices"
  page condensed: gotchas, templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity,
  defaults-not-menus, procedures-over-declarations, plan-validate-execute.
- `references/script-design.md` — The agentskills.io "using scripts" page
  condensed: agentic CLI design, structured output, error message style,
  PEP 723, uvx/npx/pipx version pinning, dry-run patterns.
- `references/this-repo-conventions.md` — Conventions specific to *this*
  repository: where to put local vs vendor skills, how the 5-level skill
  search works, AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md sync, where mirrored scripts live.

## Gotchas

- **AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md** — edit either one; never replace the
  symlink with a real file.
- **Skill discovery is one level deep first, then recursive up to 5 levels.**
  `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` works because of the recursive fallback. Don't
  nest skills more than 5 deep or they become invisible.
- **`bash 3.2` compatibility** is required for any script that might run on
  stock macOS. No `mapfile`, no `${var,,}` lowercasing, no `[[ -v var ]]`.
  See `references/script-design.md` for the safe subset.
- **`description` field length matters less than its trigger surface area.**
  A 200-word description that names 8 concrete contexts will outperform a
  50-word one that's beautifully concise but vague. Err on the side of more
  trigger phrases.
- **Don't write a skill that wraps something the agent already does well.**
  If a stock Claude session handles the task in one turn without help, a skill
  adds context-window cost for no gain. Test the no-skill baseline before
  investing in authoring.

## When the user is updating an existing skill (not creating new)

Same workflow, but skip step 2 (scaffold). Read the existing SKILL.md first,
identify which patterns from `references/authoring-patterns.md` are missing or
weakly applied, and propose edits one section at a time so the user can sanity
check. After edits, run lint, then offer the `skill-creator` handoff for
quantitative validation.

Perfect. Now let me compile my research findings into a comprehensive report.

## Research Report: Pueue Command Surface for Agent Integration

Based on documented sources from pueue's GitHub repository, wiki, and official documentation, here is what an LLM agent needs to know:

### 1. **Core Lifecycle Commands**

- **`pueue add [command]`** enqueues a task. Key flags (from man pages):
  - **`-l / --label TEXT`**: Attach a descriptive label (displayed in `pueue status`)
  - **`-a / --after <TASK_ID>`**: Create dependency (see #3)
  - **`-g / --group <GROUP>`**: Assign to group (defaults to "default" group if omitted)
  - **`-i / --immediate`**: Start task right away instead of queuing
  - **`--stashed`**: Add in paused state (won't auto-start)
  - **`--delay <DURATION>`**: Schedule execution later (e.g., "10min")
  - **`-p / --priority <NUM>`**: Set task priority
  - **`--escape`**: Escape special characters in command strings
  - **`--print-id`**: Output the new task ID to stdout
  - Tasks execute in "their original working directories with copied environment variables" (no explicit `--working-directory` flag documented)

- **`pueue pause [--group G]`**, **`pueue start [--group G]`**: Pause/resume tasks or groups
- **`pueue kill [task_ids]`**, **`pueue remove [task_ids]`**: Terminate or remove tasks
- Environment variables **`$PUEUE_WORKER_ID`** and **`$PUEUE_GROUP`** are injected into task execution (worker pool assignment and group name)

### 2. **Groups and Parallelism**

- **`pueue group add <NAME>`**: Create a new group
- **`pueue group remove <NAME>`**: Delete a group  
- **`pueue parallel <N> [--group G]`**: Set parallel concurrency (can be unlimited if set to `0`)
- When `--group` is omitted, the "default" group is used automatically
- Default group is built-in; no creation needed
- Groups allow resource segregation (e.g., one `io` group at 1 task, `cpu` group at 2 tasks in parallel)

### 3. **Dependencies / DAG Support**

- **`--after <TASK_ID>`** (short: **`-a`**) is the dependency flag on `pueue add`
- **Semantics**: "Tasks with this option will only be started if all specified dependencies successfully finish. Tasks with failed dependencies will fail as well."
- **No success/failure distinction**: Dependencies run only on success; failed parent → dependent marked with **`DependencyFailed`** status
- Use with **`pause_group_on_failure`** config setting to prevent new tasks from starting when any task fails

### 4. **JSON / Scripting Surface**

- **`pueue status --json`** and **`pueue log --json`** (short: **`-j`**) support JSON output
- **Available fields** (from docs.rs and usage): JSON output includes task `id`, `status`, `label`, `group` 
- **Documentation gap**: Exact JSON schema for `dependencies`, `exit_code`, `start_time`, `end_time` fields not explicitly documented in fetched sources; recommend running `pueue status --json | jq` to inspect actual output structure
- **No `--print-task-id` explicitly documented**; `--print-id` is the actual flag for stdout output (format undocumented)

### 5. **Retry / Restart**

- **`pueue restart [--in-place] [--start-immediately] [task_ids]`**
- **`--in-place`**: Restart task in its current queue position without creating a new entry
- **`--start-immediately`** (also **`--immediate`** in v4.0+): Begin execution immediately
- Default behavior (without flags): Creates a new task ID with identical command (does not reuse old ID)
- New task ID is assigned even with `--in-place --start-immediately`

### 6. **Output Retrieval**

- **`pueue log [task_id]`**: Display captured stdout/stderr (shows last few lines; use `--full` for complete output or `--lines N`)
- **`pueue follow [task_id]`**: Monitor running task output in real-time
- **Log storage**: All logs reside in **`${pueue_directory}/logs`** (e.g., `~/.local/share/pueue/logs/` on Linux)
- **No explicit stdout-only vs stderr-only flags documented** (follow flag `-e` for stderr mentioned but not fully specified)

### 7. **Daemon Lifecycle**

- **`pueued`**: Start daemon; use **`-d` or `--daemonize`** for background mode
- **Socket path**: Defaults to **`runtime_directory/pueue_${USER}.socket`** (e.g., `~/.local/share/pueue/pueue_username.socket` or `/run/user/{uid}/pueue_{user}.socket` if `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` set)
- **Config file**: Platform-specific:
  - Linux: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pueue/pueue.yml` or `~/.config/pueue/pueue.yml`
  - macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/pueue/pueue.yml`
  - Windows: `%APPDATA%\pueue\pueue.yml`
- **Daemon required**: All `pueue` client commands require a running `pueued` daemon (socket communication)
- **Config can be overridden**: `-c` flag or `PUEUE_CONFIG_PATH` environment variable

### 8. **Agent Gotchas**

1. **Default group behavior**: Omitting `--group` targets "default" group; no explicit creation needed
2. **Task failure → dependents fail**: If parent task fails, all tasks with `--after parent_id` are marked `DependencyFailed` and do not execute
3. **`pueue add` stdout unclear**: `--print-id` outputs the task ID, but exact format (plain integer vs JSON) is **not documented**; agent should test or use `pueue status --json` for reliable parsing
4. **Command escaping required**: "The command needs proper shell escaping"; recommend wrapping in single quotes or using `--escape` flag
5. **No shell aliases**: Custom rc-file aliases are not available in pueued environment; use pueue's own aliasing system (`pueue_aliases.yml`)
6. **`pause_group_on_failure` is config-level**: Not a command-line flag; must be set in `pueue.yml` to auto-pause group on task failure
7. **v4.0.0 breaking change**: Task state representation was redesigned; older state files are incompatible
8. **Windows daemonization unreliable**: Before v4.0, `pueued --daemonize` on Windows could terminate if terminal closes

---

**Undocumented or vague**: Exact JSON schema for `pueue status --json` (whether it includes per-task `dependencies` array), stdout format of `pueue add --print-id`, explicit `--working-directory` flag (tasks run in "original working directories" but no CLI override found), stderr-only retrieval, and whether `pause_group_on_failure` config key name is exact.

Sources:
- [Get started · Nukesor/pueue Wiki](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki/Get-started)
- [Groups · Nukesor/pueue Wiki](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki/Groups)
- [Configuration · Nukesor/pueue Wiki](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki/Configuration)
- [pueue-add man page](https://linuxcommandlibrary.com/man/pueue-add)
- [pueue-restart man page](https://linuxcommandlibrary.com/man/pueue-restart)
- [pueue CHANGELOG](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
- [Pueue GitHub Repository](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue)
```

# Pueue: Command-Line Task Queue Manager

## Overview

Pueue is a Rust-based CLI tool that manages shell command execution through a queue system. It features a background daemon (`pueued`) that processes tasks while allowing control from any terminal on the same machine.

## Key Features

**Scheduling & Execution:**
- Add tasks sequentially or run multiple tasks in parallel with configurable concurrency
- Reorder queued tasks and specify task dependencies
- Schedule execution at specific times

**Process Control:**
- Inspect task output easily
- Send input to running processes
- Pause/resume individual tasks or entire groups

**Reliability:**
- Queue persists to disk and survives crashes
- Logs are stored persistently
- Commands execute in their original working directories with copied environment variables

**Additional Capabilities:**
- Multiple task groups (queues) with independent parallel limits
- JSON output for programmatic integration
- Cross-platform support (Linux, macOS, Windows)
- Callback hooks for notifications

## Installation

Available through package managers, pre-built binaries, or via Cargo:
```
cargo install --locked pueue
```

## Core Commands

The tool provides commands for task management including `add`, `remove`, `start`, `pause`, `kill`, `status`, `log`, and `follow`, each with extensive options accessible via `-h` flags.

## Design Philosophy

Pueue prioritizes simplicity and human interaction over complex automation. The developers explicitly note it is "not designed to be a heavy-duty programmable task scheduler" and consider the project feature-complete, focusing now on maintenance and bug fixes.
```

## PueueWrapper Abstractions Report

**High-Level Operations:**
The wrapper exposes: task submission (`add_task`), task waiting (`wait_for_task`), group management (create/remove groups, set parallel concurrency per group), and lifecycle operations (restart, kill, pause, start, clean). All operations have both async (`PueueAsyncCore`) and sync (`PueueSyncCore`) variants.

**Dependency Model:**
PueueWrapper wraps Pueue's native `--after` dependency system directly. `TaskAddOptions.after` accepts a list of task IDs that must complete before the task runs—this enables simple sequential DAGs but not arbitrary dependency scheduling. No custom scheduler is built; the abstraction just exposes Pueue's CLI-native feature.

**Status Data Classes:**
Pydantic models parse `pueue status --json`:
- `Task`: captures id, command, group, dependencies, priority, label, status dict, path, environment variables
- `Group`: group metadata (name, config, parallel limits)
- `PueueStatus`: wraps full queue state as a dict of task_id→Task, group_name→Group, plus convenience methods like `.get_running_tasks()`, `.get_done_tasks()`, etc.
- `TaskAddOptions`: configuration for submission (working_dir, delay, group, after, priority, label, stashed)

**Waiting Patterns:**
`wait_for_task(task_id)` blocks until completion. The sync wrapper handles this by delegating to the async layer, which polls Pueue's CLI. No explicit timeout is exposed in the public API; polling happens via internal async methods. Group-level draining is implicit—you check status after cleanup operations.

**Entry Points:**
Two CLI commands: `pueue-api-server` (FastAPI REST wrapper) and `pueue-ui-server` (Streamlit web UI). Python API is through `PueueWrapper` (async) or `PueueWrapperSync` (blocking). No bespoke task pool or parallel executor abstraction—parallelism is group-level via `set_group_parallel()`.

**Key Pattern:**
Task organization centers on **groups** with configurable concurrency, lightweight **linear dependencies** via `after`, and **simple polling** through status queries. The wrapper is thin—it's a CLI bridge, not a job orchestrator.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SCRIPT_NAME — one-line description.
# Bash 3.2 compatible (works on stock macOS).

set -euo pipefail

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: SCRIPT_NAME [OPTIONS] ARGS
[paragraph description]
Options:
  --dry-run          Show what would happen without doing it.
  --help, -h         Show this help and exit.
Examples:
  SCRIPT_NAME foo
  SCRIPT_NAME --dry-run foo
Exit codes:
  0  success
  1  invalid arguments
  2  required input missing
EOF
}

log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
warn() { printf 'warn: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }

# Parse args, validate, run main()
main() {
  # Emit structured data on stdout; diagnostics on stderr.
}
```

Conventions:
- Data (JSON/structured) → `stdout`
- Diagnostics (logs, errors) → `stderr`
- Exit codes: 0=success, 1=invalid args, 2=missing input, 3+=domain-specific
- Support `--dry-run` and `--help` always
- Shell-escape with `set -euo pipefail`

```text
# Pueue: Getting Started Guide

**Pueue** is a task queue manager that lets you manage and execute commands sequentially or in parallel. Here's what you need to know:

## Starting the Daemon

Before using the client, launch the daemon:
- **Foreground**: Run `pueued` directly
- **Background**: Use `pueued -d` or `--daemonize`
- **Systemd (Linux)**: Install the service file and run `systemctl --user start pueued`
- **Windows**: Use built-in service commands with administrator privileges

## Basic Commands

**Adding tasks**: `pueue add sleep 60`

**Checking status**: `pueue` or `pueue status`

**Viewing output**: `pueue log` or `pueue follow $task_id`

## Command Syntax Tips

When adding flags, use a double dash separator: `pueue add -- ls -al /tmp/`

For commands with special characters or spaces, wrap them in quotes: `pueue add 'ls /tmp/dir\ with\ spaces/'`

The safest approach is surrounding your entire command with quotes to preserve shell syntax.

## Task Control

- **Pause/Resume**: `pueue pause` and `pueue start`
- **Parallel execution**: `pueue parallel 3` (runs up to 3 tasks simultaneously)
- **Task dependencies**: Use `--after/-a` flag when adding tasks
- **Stashed tasks**: Tasks that won't auto-start until explicitly enqueued

## Key Features

Tasks can have delays, force-start immediately, or depend on other tasks completing successfully. Environment variables like `$PUEUE_WORKER_ID` and `$PUEUE_GROUP` help with load distribution across worker pools.
```

# Pueue Groups Overview

Based on the GitHub wiki documentation, Pueue's group feature enables resource-based task organization. Here's what you need to know:

## Core Purpose

Groups allow you to segregate tasks by resource requirements. As the documentation explains, "Grouping tasks can be useful, whenever your tasks utilize different system resources." A practical example: an `io` group handling file transfers could run one task at a time, while a `cpu` group executes up to two computation-heavy processes simultaneously.

## Key Commands

**Group Management:**
- Create groups: `pueue group add cpu`
- Remove groups: `pueue group remove cpu`
- List all groups: `pueue group`

**Task Assignment:**
- Add tasks to specific groups using the `-g` flag: `pueue add -g cpu -- 'sleep 60'`
- Tasks without a specified group go to the default queue

**Parallelism Control:**
- Set concurrent tasks per group: `pueue parallel -g cpu 2`

**Monitoring & Control:**
- View specific group status: `status --group $NAME`
- Pause/resume groups: `pueue pause -g cpu`

This approach prevents system bottlenecks while optimizing resource utilization across different task types.
```

# Pueue Advanced Usage Summary

Based on the wiki page, Pueue offers several advanced features:

## Key Capabilities

**Aliases**: Users can define command shortcuts in `pueue_aliases.yml`. The system checks the first word of commands for matches, enabling quick access to frequently-used operations.

**Callbacks**: Tasks can trigger notifications upon completion. As stated, "You can specify a callback that will be called every time a task finishes." The system supports variables like `{{ id }}`, `{{ result }}`, `{{ exit_code }}`, and `{{ output }}` for customization across notification systems (Linux, macOS, etc.).

**JSON Output**: "The Pueue client `status` and `log` commands support JSON output with the `-j` flag," enabling integration with external tools like `jq` for filtering and processing.

**Interactive Fuzzy-Finding**: The wiki includes shell functions using `fzf` and `bat` for interactive task management with keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+p for pause, Ctrl+s for start, etc.).

**Shell Completions**: Pueue generates completion files for Zsh, Bash, and Fish shells via the `pueue completions` command.

**Logging**: All logs reside in `${pueue_directory}/logs`, with debugging available through verbose flags (`-vvvv`).

The documentation emphasizes practical examples, including wget progress monitoring and jq-based status summarization for queue management.
```

1	---
2	name: agent-history-hygiene
3	description: Commit SpecStory chat transcripts (`.specstory/history/*.md`), Claude Code plan files (`.claude/plans/*.md`, `plansDirectory`), and other coding-agent artifacts (`.cursor/plans/`, `.cursor/rules/`, `.opencode/plans/`, `.specify/`, `.codex/`) alongside the feature diff they produced — without leaking `.env` contents, API keys, or private-key PEM blocks into git history. Use when the user says "commit my chat", "save this specstory session", "stage the plan file", "scrub the transcript", "my .env leaked in chat", "bootstrap pre-commit for this project", or when you notice untracked `.specstory/history/*.md` or `.claude/plans/*.md` files while running `git status`. Also use after an accidental push of a secret to enforce rotate-first, rewrite-last remediation instead of reflexive `git push --force`.
4	---
5	
6	# agent-history-hygiene
7	
8	Keep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the
9	code they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the
10	`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.
11	
12	Three surfaces, separated by purpose:
13	
14	| Surface                          | Question it answers                                          |
15	|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
16	| `find-session.sh`                | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?"      |
17	| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`       | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?"               |
18	| `bootstrap-project.sh`           | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a repo?" |
19	| `scan-staged.sh`                 | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?"      |
20	| `references/remediation.md`      | "I already pushed a secret — now what?"                      |
21	
22	## Core invariants
23	
24	1. **Agent transcripts and plan files are committed alongside the diff
25	   that produced them.** Never add them to `.gitignore`. An agent that
26	   drops these from a commit has broken the user's review trail.
27	2. **Rotate at the provider before any git rewrite.** The only act
28	   that revokes a leaked credential is rotation. History rewriting
29	   scrubs bytes on one clone and leaves them on every other.
30	3. **`git push --force` against a shared branch is never the fix for a
31	   leak.** At best it's useless; at worst it destroys teammate work and
32	   silently re-introduces the secret when someone merges their old
33	   history back.
34	
35	## When to use this skill
36	
37	Use it when the user (or you) surface any of:
38	
39	- "Commit my chat" / "save the specstory session" / "include the plan
40	  file in this commit" / "把 plan 跟 specstory 一起 commit 進去".
41	- You see dirty `.specstory/history/*.md`, `.claude/plans/*.md`,
42	  `.cursor/plans/*.md`, or any other configured agent artifact during
43	  `git status` and you're about to commit a feature.
44	- "Scrub this transcript" / "redact my key" / "gitleaks flagged my
45	  chat history".
46	- "Set up pre-commit for this repo" / "I'm starting a new project — how
47	  do I get the hook stack?" / "bootstrap secret scanning here".
48	- "I pushed a `.env`" / "a secret went to main" / "do I need to force
49	  push?" — the agent must steer to `references/remediation.md` and
50	  stop the user from force-pushing reflexively.
51	
52	## When NOT to use
53	
54	- The user explicitly wants agent transcripts **excluded** from the
55	  repo. Respect that; suggest a one-liner `.gitignore` addition and
56	  skip this skill entirely.
57	- The leak is already on a shared `main`/release branch. Do **not**
58	  offer to rewrite history — jump to `references/remediation.md` §5.
59	- The project genuinely has no agent session (no `.specstory/`, no
60	  `.claude/plans/`, etc.). Nothing to stage.
61	- Single-file, single-commit hygiene that the agent handles without any
62	  script (e.g., adding a missing trailing newline).
63	
64	## Integration with existing infrastructure
65	
66	This skill sits **on top of** any chezmoi-managed stack the user
67	already has. It does not duplicate:
68	
69	- **chezmoi's global `core.hooksPath`** (`~/.config/git/hooks/pre-commit`)
70	  — that wrapper runs the repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and then
71	  optionally `gitleaks git --staged`. The skill bootstraps the repo-level
72	  config the wrapper expects to find.
73	- **chezmoi's `.gitleaks.toml`** — the user's config already carries
74	  curated rules for common API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Supabase,
75	  Linear, WakaTime, Cursor, HuggingFace, Notion, Tailscale, Clash /
76	  V2Ray tokens). The skill's `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` ships the
77	  same rule IDs so `.gitleaksignore` / allowlist tweaks stay portable.
78	- **chezmoi's `scripts/redact_secrets.py`** — remains the upstream
79	  source of truth. The skill bundles a copy so non-chezmoi users get
80	  protection; sync procedure in
81	  [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md).
82	
83	What this skill **adds**:
84	
85	- Agent-facing discipline (this `SKILL.md` + `references/remediation.md`).
86	- A single-command project bootstrap (`bootstrap-project.sh`) for repos
87	  without chezmoi or where the user wants the stack in one go.
88	- Session-discovery heuristics (`find-session.sh`) for the "find my
89	  current transcript among many" problem.
90	- An exit-code wrapper (`scan-staged.sh`) agents can branch on before
91	  committing.
92	
93	## Workflow A: commit-time hygiene
94	
95	Default flow when the agent is about to commit feature changes plus
96	chat/plan artifacts.
97	
98	```bash
99	# 1. Make sure the agent knows which session is "ours" — mostly
100	#    relevant when multiple Claude/SpecStory sessions run in the repo.
101	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/find-session.sh
102	
103	# 2. Stage code the usual way, then auto-add agent artifacts.
104	git add path/to/feature/file.ts
105	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh
106	# Use --session-only if you want ONLY the current SpecStory + newest plan;
107	# default stages every dirty *.md in every configured agent dir.
108	
109	# 3. Belt-and-suspenders secret scan before commit. Exit 0 = clean.
110	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh || {
111	  # Exit 10/20: leaks found. Jump to references/remediation.md.
112	  echo "Leaks detected — see references/remediation.md before committing." >&2
113	  exit 1
114	}
115	
116	# 4. Commit. pre-commit (installed by bootstrap) runs redact-agent-secrets
117	#    then gitleaks again as a catch-all.
118	git commit -m "feat: ..."
119	```
120	
121	## Workflow B: bootstrap a new project
122	
123	For repos that don't yet have `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitleaks.toml`
124	installed. Runs once per repo.
125	
126	```bash
127	cd /path/to/new/project
128	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh \
129	  --install-hook            # optional: auto-stage on every commit
130	
131	# Verify: shake out any existing issues in the working tree.
132	pre-commit run --all-files
133	```
134	
135	What `bootstrap-project.sh` does:
136	
137	1. Drops `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the repo
138	   (skips if already present unless `--force`).
139	2. Writes `scripts/redact_secrets.py` (bundled copy; use
140	   `--from-chezmoi` to symlink the chezmoi source so fixes propagate).
141	3. Runs `pre-commit install` (or `uvx pre-commit@4 install` if
142	   pre-commit isn't on `PATH`).
143	4. Audits `.gitignore` / `.git/info/exclude` for patterns that would
144	   silently hide an agent artifact dir — warns without editing.
145	5. Checks `~/.claude/settings.json` for `plansDirectory`; prints the
146	   one-line patch if missing.
147	6. With `--install-hook`: writes a `prepare-commit-msg` hook that calls
148	   `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only --allow-empty` so every
149	   `git commit` auto-attaches the current session file.
150	
151	## Workflow C: post-leak remediation
152	
153	When `scan-staged.sh` reports exit `10`/`20`, or the user says "I
154	committed / pushed a secret":
155	
156	1. **STOP** the user from running `git push --force` reflexively.
157	2. Read `references/remediation.md` end-to-end.
158	3. Walk the user through **step 1 (rotate)** regardless of blast
159	   radius. Only after rotation does the question of scrubbing history
160	   become worth discussing.
161	4. Use the decision tree in the runbook to pick the right git action.
162	
163	## Gotchas
164	
165	- **`plansDirectory` project-level sometimes ignored.** Claude Code
166	  issue [#19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537)
167	  reports project-level `plansDirectory` being ignored in some
168	  versions. After running a `/plan`, verify the file actually landed
169	  where you expected before relying on `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`
170	  picking it up. User-level config (`~/.claude/settings.json` with
171	  `"plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"`) is the recommended default.
172	- **`gitleaks protect` is deprecated.** Since v8.19.0 use
173	  `gitleaks git --staged --redact` (pre-commit) and
174	  `gitleaks dir <path>` (working directory). The older commands still
175	  work but emit a deprecation notice. This skill uses the modern
176	  syntax everywhere.
177	- **`pre-commit install` is per-clone.** Each teammate must run
178	  `pre-commit install` in their own clone for hooks to fire. CI cannot
179	  be trusted as the single gate — it's second-chance, not last-chance.
180	- **Transcript files can be huge.** A long SpecStory session can exceed
181	  2 MB. The template bumps `check-added-large-files` to `--maxkb=2048`
182	  to avoid false positives, but a very long session can still overflow.
183	  If you hit the limit, rotate sessions (`specstory run claude`
184	  creates a fresh file) instead of raising the cap further.
185	- **Session-UUID divergence between SpecStory CLI and VS Code
186	  extension.** The extension autosaves into `.specstory/history/`
187	  continuously; the CLI (`specstory run claude`) creates one file per
188	  invocation. If both are active you can end up with two transcripts
189	  for what feels like "one session" — mtime-newest wins in
190	  `find-session.sh`.
191	- **Global `core.hooksPath` means bare repos aren't protected.** The
192	  chezmoi setup's global hook runs `.pre-commit-config.yaml` IF it
193	  exists — so a repo without `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has no
194	  protection. Run `bootstrap-project.sh` before the first commit with
195	  agent artifacts, not after.
196	
197	## Available scripts
198	
199	- **`scripts/find-session.sh [--format=specstory|claude|both] [--json]`**
200	  Discover the current agent session files for `$PWD`. TSV default,
201	  `--json` for structured callers. Never exits non-zero (always 0,
202	  empty fields signal absence).
203	
204	- **`scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--session-only] [--include-all-plans] [--dry-run] [--allow-empty]`**
205	  `git add` the right agent artifacts before the next commit.
206	  `--session-only` stages only the current SpecStory + newest plan;
207	  default stages every dirty `*.md` in every configured artifact dir.
208	  Refuses to run if there are no code changes (prevents "commit just
209	  transcript"); override with `--allow-empty`.
210	
211	- **`scripts/scan-staged.sh [--redact] [--verbose]`**
212	  Run `gitleaks git --staged` with agent-friendly exit codes
213	  (0 clean / 10 redacted / 20 leaks / 30 gitleaks missing). JSON lines
214	  on stdout, prose diagnostics on stderr.
215	
216	- **`scripts/bootstrap-project.sh [--from-chezmoi] [--install-hook] [--force] [--dry-run]`**
217	  Install `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` + the redactor
218	  into the current repo, then run `pre-commit install`. Audits
219	  `.gitignore` and `~/.claude/settings.json` for misconfigurations
220	  (warns, never silently edits).
221	
222	## Bundled assets
223	
224	- `assets/artifact-dirs.txt` — the canonical list of agent artifact
225	  directories (SpecStory, Claude plans, Cursor plans + rules, OpenCode
226	  plans, Spec-kit, Codex). Consumed by `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` and
227	  by `bootstrap-project.sh` when rendering the pre-commit `files:`
228	  regex.
229	- `assets/pre-commit-config.yaml.template` — minimal
230	  `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with `redact-agent-secrets` + gitleaks +
231	  standard hygiene hooks.
232	- `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` — portable subset of the chezmoi
233	  `.gitleaks.toml` with custom rule IDs + a path-scoped allowlist for
234	  agent artifact dirs.
235	- `assets/redact_secrets.py` — bundled copy of chezmoi's
236	  `scripts/redact_secrets.py`. Chezmoi version is upstream; sync doc
237	  in `references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`.
238	
239	## Reference files
240	
241	- [`references/transcript-session-discovery.md`](references/transcript-session-discovery.md)
242	  — SpecStory / Claude session layouts and the `$PWD → slug` algorithm.
243	  Read when `find-session.sh` returns empty or ambiguous results.
244	- [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md)
245	  — three-layer defense (redact → gitleaks → `scan-staged.sh`),
246	  allowlist design, sync procedure for the bundled redactor. Read

248	- [`references/remediation.md`](references/remediation.md) —
249	  rotate-first runbook for "I committed / pushed a secret". Read
250	  **before** any `git filter-repo` / `git push --force` action.
251	
252	## Tests
253	
254	The skill ships with a three-level test suite under
255	[`tests/`](tests/README.md). Run from repo root:
256	
257	```bash
258	make test-skill
259	```
260	
261	- `test_redact_secrets.py` — pytest for pure redactor functions.
262	- `test_gitleaks_corpus.py` — golden-corpus fixtures staged in tmp git
263	  repos, asserting real-key shapes fire and example shapes are
264	  allowlisted only inside configured artifact dirs.
265	- `test_scan_staged.sh` — exit-code contract for
266	  `scripts/scan-staged.sh` (0 / 20 / 30 / 2).
267	
268	The corpus + shell tests skip gracefully when `gitleaks` isn't on
269	`PATH`. See [`tests/README.md`](tests/README.md) for what each
270	regression the suite locks in.
271	
272	## Related skills
273	
274	- [`project-knowledge-harness`](../project-knowledge-harness/SKILL.md)
275	  — complementary memory harness (TODO.md + backlog/ + pitfalls/) that
276	  references `.claude/plans/` as "ephemeral agent scratchpads". This
277	  skill fills the gap: those scratchpads belong in git, not ignored.

```

```text
1	---
2	name: dvc-ml-workflow
3	description: Set up and operate a DVC (Data Version Control) workflow for ML projects — `dvc init`, `dvc.yaml` pipelines, `params.yaml`, `dvc exp run --queue` for parallel sweeps with metrics auto-bound to ephemeral git commits, and remote storage (S3/SSH/GDrive). Use whenever the user wants reproducible ML pipelines, data/model versioning that lives alongside git, parameter sweeps without standing up a tracking server, queued/parallel experiment execution, or asks about `dvc.yaml` / `dvc exp run` / `dvc queue` / `params.yaml` / `dvc add` / `dvc push` / `.dvc/cache`. Always references the official docs at https://dvc.org/doc and the upstream repo https://github.com/treeverse/dvc (Iterative was acquired by Treeverse in 2024 — `pip install dvc` resolves to this repo).
4	---
5	
6	# DVC ML Workflow
7	
8	DVC turns a git repo into a full ML lab: data and model files are versioned out-of-band (in a cache + remote), pipelines are declared in `dvc.yaml`, and experiments are run as ephemeral git commits with metrics and plots attached. No tracking server, no separate database — everything lives in your existing git history.
9	
10	This skill is opinionated about **the parts of DVC that matter for production ML work**: pipelines, queued experiments, metrics/commit binding, and remotes. It defers to the official docs at https://dvc.org/doc for everything else and links them inline so the agent always pulls the latest guidance.
11	
12	## When to use
13	
14	- User wants reproducible ML pipelines without a tracking server (`mlflow`, `wandb`, etc.)
15	- User mentions `dvc.yaml`, `params.yaml`, `dvc exp run`, `dvc queue`, `dvc push`, `.dvc/cache`
16	- User wants to do a hyperparameter sweep / grid search and have each run land as a separate commit with metrics
17	- User wants to version a dataset or model file too large for git
18	- User asks "how do I make my training reproducible" and is already on git
19	- User wants `mlflow ui`-style experiment comparison but **doesn't want to run a server** (DVC's `dvc exp show` + VS Code extension fills that role)
20	
21	## When NOT to use
22	
23	- User wants a hosted experiment dashboard with multi-user collaboration → use `mlflow-tracking` skill
24	- User wants LLM trace observability (spans, prompts, token costs) → DVC has no story here; use `mlflow-tracking`
25	- User just needs `git lfs` for a few large files → DVC is overkill; recommend `git lfs`
26	- User has an existing `mlflow` workflow and is happy with it → don't push DVC unless they ask
27	
28	## Authoritative sources (always link these, don't paraphrase from memory)
29	
30	- Docs root: https://dvc.org/doc
31	- Command reference: https://dvc.org/doc/command-reference
32	- User guide: https://dvc.org/doc/user-guide
33	- Upstream repo: https://github.com/treeverse/dvc (formerly `iterative/dvc`; redirects)
34	- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/dvc/
35	
36	When you're unsure of a flag, syntax, or behavior, **fetch the relevant doc page** rather than guessing — DVC's CLI surface changes between minor versions.
37	
38	## Core mental model
39	
40	Three orthogonal things, often confused:
41	
42	| DVC concept | Analogy | What it does |
43	|---|---|---|
44	| `dvc add <file>` | `git lfs track` | Snapshots a single file/dir into the cache, writes a `.dvc` pointer file (which **is** committed to git) |
45	| `dvc.yaml` (stages) | `Makefile` | Declares pipeline stages with dependencies and outputs; `dvc repro` re-runs only stages whose inputs changed |
46	| `dvc exp run` | `git commit` for experiments | Runs the pipeline once with optional param overrides, captures metrics + outputs as an **ephemeral commit** |
47	
48	The non-obvious bit: `dvc exp run` builds on top of `dvc.yaml`. You don't choose between "use pipelines" and "run experiments" — you write the pipeline once, then launch many experiments against it.
49	
50	## Workflow
51	
52	### 1. Initialize the project
53	
54	Use the bundled helper (handles `.gitignore`, sample files, optional remote):
55	
56	```bash
57	bash skills/local/dvc-ml-workflow/scripts/init-dvc-project.sh
58	# or with a remote:
59	bash skills/local/dvc-ml-workflow/scripts/init-dvc-project.sh --remote s3://my-bucket/dvc-store
60	```
61	
62	Manual equivalent (only do this if the helper doesn't fit):
63	
64	```bash
65	dvc init                              # creates .dvc/, .dvcignore
66	git add .dvc .dvcignore
67	git commit -m "Initialize DVC"
68	```
69	
70	For a sub-project inside a monorepo that already has its own `.git`, use `dvc init --subdir`. See [Gotchas](#gotchas).
71	
72	### 2. Track data and models
73	
74	```bash
75	dvc add data/raw/             # snapshot a directory
76	dvc add models/best.pt        # snapshot a single model file
77	git add data/raw.dvc models/best.pt.dvc .gitignore
78	git commit -m "Track raw data and best model"
79	```
80	
81	The `.dvc` files are tiny pointers (md5 + path). The actual bytes go to `.dvc/cache/`. **Never** `git add` anything inside `.dvc/cache/` — it's gitignored automatically and would defeat the purpose.
82	
83	### 3. Define a pipeline (`dvc.yaml`)
84	
85	Use `params.yaml` for hyperparameters. Use `dvc stage add` to declare stages — never hand-edit `dvc.yaml` from scratch unless you've already used `dvc stage add` enough times to know the schema.
86	
87	```bash
88	dvc stage add -n featurize \
89	  -d src/featurize.py -d data/raw \
90	  -o data/features \
91	  python src/featurize.py
92	
93	dvc stage add -n train \
94	  -d src/train.py -d data/features -p model.lr,model.epochs \
95	  -o models/best.pt \
96	  -M metrics.json --plots-no-cache plots.csv \
97	  python src/train.py
98	```
99	
100	The `-M` flag marks a file as a **metrics file** (auto-bound to the experiment commit). `--plots-no-cache` marks a file as a plot source (rendered by `dvc plots show`).
101	
102	For schema details and `foreach` matrix stages, **read** `references/pipelines-and-stages.md`.
103	
104	### 4. Run experiments (the queue is the killer feature)
105	
106	For a single run:
107	
108	```bash
109	dvc exp run                           # uses current params.yaml
110	dvc exp run -S model.lr=1e-3          # override one param
111	dvc exp run -S 'model.lr=range(1e-4,1e-2,3)'  # NOT valid — see queue below
112	```
113	
114	For a **sweep**, queue + start workers:
115	
116	```bash
117	# Enqueue a grid (each -S adds one experiment to the queue):
118	dvc exp run --queue -S model.lr=1e-4
119	dvc exp run --queue -S model.lr=5e-4
120	dvc exp run --queue -S model.lr=1e-3
121	
122	# Start 3 parallel workers — they each pick one queued experiment:
123	dvc queue start --jobs 3
124	
125	# Watch progress:
126	dvc queue status
127	dvc queue logs <task-id>             # if one fails
128	
129	# When done:
130	dvc exp show                          # tabular view of all experiments
131	```
132	
133	Each completed experiment is an **ephemeral commit** in `refs/exps/...`. Metrics, params, and outputs are bundled with it. Promote one to a real commit with `dvc exp apply <exp-name>` then `git commit`.
134	
135	For grids, queue helpers, and ephemeral-vs-real commit semantics, **read** `references/experiments-and-queue.md`.
136	
137	### 5. Push artifacts to a remote
138	
139	```bash
140	dvc remote add -d origin s3://my-bucket/dvc-store    # -d = default
141	dvc push                                             # upload cache to remote
142	git push                                             # share the .dvc pointers
143	```
144	
145	Anyone who clones can `dvc pull` to get the actual bytes. For S3 / GCS / Azure / SSH / GDrive specifics and credential handling, **read** `references/data-and-remotes.md`.
146	
147	### 6. Compare and visualize
148	
149	```bash
150	dvc exp show                          # table of all experiments
151	dvc exp show --csv | column -t -s,    # human-readable
152	dvc metrics show                      # current workspace metrics
153	dvc metrics diff HEAD~1               # compare against last commit
154	dvc plots show                        # render plots from --plots files
155	dvc plots diff HEAD~1                 # overlay current vs prior plots
156	```
157	
158	For plot templates (Vega-Lite), confusion matrices, and the VS Code extension, **read** `references/plots-and-metrics.md`.
159	
160	## Available scripts
161	
162	- **`scripts/init-dvc-project.sh`** — Idempotent project init. `dvc init` + `.gitignore` for `.dvc/cache/` + optional `dvc remote add` + drops the `dvc.yaml` / `params.yaml` / `.dvcignore` templates from `assets/` if missing.
163	  - Flags: `--remote URL`, `--subdir`, `--force`, `--dry-run`, `--help`
164	- **`scripts/queue-helper.sh`** — Wraps `dvc queue` subcommands with structured JSON stdout (one object per task) so an agent can grep/filter task status without parsing tabular output.
165	  - Subcommands: `enqueue PARAM=VAL,...`, `start --jobs N`, `status`, `logs TASK_ID`
166	  - Flags: `--help`, `--json` (default for `status`)
167	- **`scripts/lint-dvcyaml.sh`** — Validates `dvc.yaml` by running `dvc dag --dot` (parse-only, no execution). Exits non-zero with the parse error if the schema is broken.
168	  - Flags: `--help`
169	
170	## Bundled assets
171	
172	- `assets/dvc.yaml.template` — Minimal 2-stage pipeline (`featurize` → `train`) with metrics and plots wired up correctly.
173	- `assets/params.yaml.template` — Nested params for `data` / `model` / `train` sections (the `-S model.lr=...` override syntax keys off this nesting).
174	- `assets/.dvcignore.template` — Sensible defaults: ignore notebooks, scratch dirs, `__pycache__`, etc.
175	
176	## Reference files
177	
178	- `references/pipelines-and-stages.md` — Read **when** writing or debugging `dvc.yaml`: stage schema, `foreach`, `vars`, `wdir`, `frozen`, `always_changed`, and the difference between `-d` / `-o` / `-M` / `--plots`.
179	- `references/experiments-and-queue.md` — Read **when** the user wants sweeps, parallel runs, or asks how metrics get bound to commits. Covers `dvc exp run --queue`, `dvc queue start --jobs`, `dvc exp apply` / `branch` / `remove` / `gc`, and ephemeral-commit semantics.
180	- `references/data-and-remotes.md` — Read **when** setting up `dvc remote` or troubleshooting `dvc push` / `dvc pull`. Covers S3, SSH, GDrive, Azure, GCS, MinIO (S3-compatible), credentials via env / `dvc remote modify --local`.
181	- `references/plots-and-metrics.md` — Read **when** the user asks about visualization, dashboards, or VS Code integration. Covers `dvc plots show / diff`, custom Vega-Lite templates, confusion matrices, and `dvc.api.metrics_show()` for programmatic access.
182	
183	## Gotchas
184	
185	- **`dvc init` fails inside an existing repo's subdirectory** unless you pass `--subdir`. Symptom: `ERROR: '.git' or '.hg' directory not found`. The helper script handles this — manually, do `dvc init --subdir`.
186	- **`dvc exp run --queue` only enqueues; it does not run.** Until you call `dvc queue start`, queued experiments sit idle. The agent will sometimes report "experiment finished" because the enqueue succeeded — verify with `dvc queue status`.
187	- **`dvc.lock` MUST be committed.** It records the exact md5s of inputs/outputs for each stage. If you `.gitignore` it, `dvc repro` becomes non-deterministic between machines. Conversely, **`.dvc/cache/` MUST NOT be committed** (it's the actual data — that goes to the remote).
188	- **Metrics file format matters.** `-M metrics.json` expects a flat JSON object (`{"acc": 0.91, "loss": 0.3}`) or a one-level-nested one. YAML works too. Free-form text won't render in `dvc exp show`.
189	- **`dvc push` silently succeeds if the remote is misconfigured but credentials are missing** for some backends — it just reports "0 files pushed" without an error code in older versions. Always verify with `dvc status -c` (cloud status) after the first push from a new machine.
190	- **Param overrides use dot-notation against `params.yaml` keys.** `-S lr=1e-3` only works if `lr` is at the top level. If you nested it under `model:`, you must use `-S model.lr=1e-3`.
191	- **macOS port 8080 / Iterative Studio**: if the user mentions Iterative Studio, note that it's now a separate Treeverse-managed product, not bundled with `dvc` itself. Don't conflate the two.
192	- **`dvc queue start` runs jobs in the background.** Closing your terminal does NOT kill them (they're detached). Use `dvc queue kill <task-id>` to stop one.
193
```

3	description: Prepare a marimo notebook to run as both an interactive UI and a scheduled batch script, using Tyro for CLI parsing (with dataclass or Pydantic params) and MLflow for experiment tracking. 5	
6	# marimo-batch-mlflow
7	
8	Opinionated fork of [marimo-team/skills/marimo-batch](https://github.com/marimo-team/skills/tree/main/skills/marimo-batch) that:
9	
10	1. Uses **[Tyro](https://brentyi.github.io/tyro/)** for CLI parsing (works with `dataclass`, `pydantic.BaseModel`, or `attrs`) instead of `mo.cli_args()` + manual help-table rendering.
11	2. Uses **[MLflow](https://mlflow.org/)** + **[mlflow-widgets](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/mlflow-widgets)** for experiment tracking instead of Weights and Biases.
12	3. Keeps the dual-mode pattern (`mo.app_meta().mode == "script"`) so a single `notebook.py` is both the UI for iteration and the entry point for `uv run notebook.py --epochs 50` batch jobs.
13	
14	## When to use this vs upstream `marimo-batch`
15	
16	| Concern | upstream `marimo-batch` | this skill |
17	|---|---|---|
18	| CLI parsing | `mo.cli_args()` + hand-rolled `rich.Table` for `--help` | `tyro.cli(ModelParams)` — auto `--help`, type coercion, validation |
19	| Params model | Pydantic `BaseModel` | `dataclass` (primary) or `pydantic.BaseModel` (alternative) |
20	| Tracking backend | Weights and Biases (`wandb`) | MLflow (`mlflow` + optional `mlflow-widgets` for live charts) |
21	| Live training UI | none — W&B web dashboard only | `mlflow_widgets.MlflowChart` cell, gated off in script mode |
22	| Grid launcher | HF Jobs + `WANDB_API_KEY` secret | HF Jobs + `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` (+ optional `MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN`) |
23	
24	Pick this skill when the user has a self-hosted MLflow server (or local `./mlruns` is fine) and prefers strongly-typed CLIs. Pick upstream when the user is already on W&B.
25	
26	## Dual-mode pattern
27	
28	The single source-of-truth idiom: branch on `mo.app_meta().mode == "script"` once, build `params` either from a form or from CLI flags, then **let every downstream cell consume `params` regardless of source**.
29	
30	```python
31	import marimo as mo
32	
33	is_script_mode = mo.app_meta().mode == "script"
34	
35	if is_script_mode:
36	    params = tyro.cli(ModelParams)
37	else:
38	    mo.stop(form.value is None, mo.md("*Submit the form to start training.*"))
39	    params = ModelParams(**form.value)
40	
41	# Every cell below uses `params.epochs`, `params.batch_size`, ...
42	# unaware of which branch produced it.
43	```
44	
45	This is what makes the notebook usable as both a UI for fast iteration and a CLI script for sweeps without code duplication.
46	
47	## Params with dataclass + Tyro (primary)
48	
49	```python
50	from dataclasses import dataclass
51	import tyro
52	
53	@dataclass
54	class ModelParams:
55	    """Model training parameters."""
56	    epochs: int = 25
57	    """Number of training epochs."""
58	    batch_size: int = 32
59	    """Training batch size."""
60	    learning_rate: float = 1e-4
61	    """Learning rate for AdamW."""
62	    mlflow_experiment: str = "batch-sizes"
63	    """MLflow experiment name (empty string disables logging)."""
64	    mlflow_run_name: str | None = None
65	    """Optional explicit run name; auto-derived from params if None."""
66	
67	if is_script_mode:
68	    params = tyro.cli(ModelParams)
69	```
70	
71	Tyro derives `--epochs INT`, `--batch-size INT`, etc., from the field names; PEP 257 docstrings under each field become CLI help text. `--help` is generated automatically — no `rich.Table` boilerplate needed.
72	
73	CLI usage:
74	
75	```bash
76	uv run notebook.py --epochs 50 --batch-size 64 --learning-rate 5e-4
77	uv run notebook.py --help     # auto-generated
78	```
79	
80	## Params with Pydantic (alternative)
81	
82	Tyro v0.8+ supports `pydantic.BaseModel` directly. Trade `dataclass` for Pydantic when you need field-level validators or `@computed_field`:
83	
84	```python
85	from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
86	import tyro
87	
88	class ModelParams(BaseModel):
89	    epochs: int = Field(default=25, description="Number of training epochs.")
90	    batch_size: int = Field(default=32, description="Training batch size.")
91	    learning_rate: float = Field(default=1e-4, description="Learning rate.")
92	    mlflow_experiment: str = Field(default="batch-sizes")
93	
94	params = tyro.cli(ModelParams)  # same call site
95	```
96	
97	`Field(description=...)` becomes CLI help. See [`references/params-pydantic.py`](references/params-pydantic.py) for the cell-level diff against the dataclass version.
98	
99	## MLflow tracking
100	
101	Wrap the training loop in `mlflow.start_run()`. Default to graceful degradation when `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` is unset (MLflow falls back to `./mlruns/`). Disable logging entirely by setting `params.mlflow_experiment = ""`.
102	
103	```python
104	import mlflow
105	import os
106	
107	tracking_uri = os.environ.get("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI")
108	if tracking_uri:
109	    mlflow.set_tracking_uri(tracking_uri)
110	if params.mlflow_experiment:
111	    mlflow.set_experiment(params.mlflow_experiment)
112	
113	run_ctx = mlflow.start_run(run_name=params.mlflow_run_name) if params.mlflow_experiment else None
114	
115	if run_ctx:
116	    mlflow.log_params({k: v for k, v in vars(params).items() if not k.startswith("mlflow_")})
117	
118	for epoch in range(params.epochs):
119	    avg_loss = train_one_epoch(...)
120	    if run_ctx:
121	        mlflow.log_metric("loss", avg_loss, step=epoch)
122	
123	if run_ctx:
124	    mlflow.end_run()
125	```
126	
127	Use `with mlflow.start_run(...) as run:` if you don't need conditional disable.
128	
129	## Live training widget (UI mode only)
130	
131	In edit mode, embed `mlflow_widgets.MlflowChart` so the user sees the loss curve update live as the training cell runs. Gate it off in script mode (no display surface):
132	
133	```python
134	from mlflow_widgets import MlflowChart
135	
136	if not is_script_mode and params.mlflow_experiment:
137	    chart = MlflowChart(
138	        tracking_uri=os.environ.get("MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI", "file:./mlruns"),
139	        experiment_name=params.mlflow_experiment,
140	        metric_key="loss",
141	    )
142	    widget = mo.ui.anywidget(chart)
143	    widget
144	```
145	
146	For comparing finished runs, swap `MlflowChart` → `MlflowRunTable` or `MlflowParallelCoordinates`. See [mlflow-widgets README](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/mlflow-widgets) for the full surface.
147

157	    EnvConfig({
158	        "MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI": lambda u: mlflow.MlflowClient(tracking_uri=u).search_experiments(),
159	        "MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN": lambda _: True,  # presence-only check

179

181	
182	For hyperparameter sweeps point users at [`references/grid.py`](references/grid.py). Same contract as upstream:

184	- Dry run by default: `uv run grid.py` prints sampled combinations.

6	# mkdocs-site-bootstrap
7	
8	Bootstrap and (optionally) deploy a MkDocs Material documentation site for a
9	repository, then keep helping the user add pages over time.

11	This skill is **consent-gated**. It records the user's preferences in
12	`.skills/preferences.yaml` and never repeats destructive actions without
13	asking. If the user changes their mind, `scripts/check-preferences.sh --reset
14	mkdocs_site_bootstrap` clears the recorded decision so the next invocation

18

32	- User wants to author a new agent skill → use `skill-author`

35	
36	### 1. Read preferences first
37	
38	Before doing anything, check whether this repo already has a recorded
39	decision:
40	
41	```bash

44	```

50	| File doesn't exist or key missing | Never asked | Proceed to step 2 (interview) |
51	| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: true` | Site is live | Skip to step 6 (ongoing helpers) |
52	| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: false` | Bootstrapped but not deployed | Skip to step 5 (deploy) |

3	description: Set up and operate MLflow for ML experiment tracking, model registry, and LLM tracing in any Python project. 5	
6	# MLflow Tracking
7	
8	MLflow gives you experiment tracking, a model registry, and (since 2.14+) first-class LLM observability — all from one Python library + UI. Unlike DVC it **does** require a tracking backend (file / SQLite / server), but it gives you a real dashboard and multi-user collaboration in return.
9	
10	This skill is opinionated about the **three deployment modes that actually get used in practice**, with a vendored production stack you can copy into any project. It defers to the official docs for everything else.
11	
12	## When to use
13	
14	- User wants to track ML experiments (params, metrics, artifacts) with a UI
15	- User mentions `mlflow.start_run`, `mlflow.log_metric`, `mlflow.set_tracking_uri`, `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI`, `mlflow ui`
16	- User wants framework autologging (sklearn / PyTorch / Lightning / XGBoost / LightGBM / Keras / TensorFlow / Transformers / spark)
17	- User wants LLM trace observability (OpenAI, Anthropic, LangChain, LlamaIndex, DSPy, AutoGen, CrewAI, etc.)
18	- User wants to spin up a self-hosted tracking server with PostgreSQL + MinIO (production)
19	- User wants a model registry with aliases (Champion / Challenger / Production)
20	- User asks "how do I compare runs", "where do my logged params go", "how do I serve a logged model"
21	
22	## When NOT to use
23	
24	- User wants reproducible **pipelines** with data versioning → use `dvc-ml-workflow` skill
25	- User wants Weights & Biases specifically → MLflow is the open-source counterpart but not a drop-in replacement
26	- User wants DataBricks-managed MLflow → most code transfers, but auth/workspace setup is Databricks-specific; defer to Databricks docs
27	- User wants a single throwaway run with no UI → `print()` is fine; MLflow adds overhead
28	
29	## Authoritative sources (link these, don't paraphrase from memory)
30	
31	- Docs root: https://mlflow.org/docs/latest
32	- Tracking: https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/tracking.html
33	- Model Registry: https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/model-registry.html
34	- LLM tracing / GenAI: https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/llms/tracing/index.html
35	- Autologging matrix: https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/tracking/autolog.html
36	- Upstream repo: https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow
37	- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/mlflow/
38	- mlflow-widgets (anywidget for live charts): https://github.com/daviddwlee84/mlflow-widgets
39	
40	MLflow ships a release roughly every 4–6 weeks. **Fetch the docs page** before answering version-specific questions (especially anything about LLM tracing, which is the fastest-moving area).
41	
42	## Decision: which deployment mode?
43	
44	Pick **before** writing any code. Switching later means migrating runs.
45	
46	| Mode | Tracking URI | When to choose | Read |
47	|---|---|---|---|
48	| **File** | `file:./mlruns` (default) | One-off experiments, no UI needed, no model registry | — |
49	| **SQLite + `mlflow ui`** ⭐ | `sqlite:///mlflow.db` | Solo work, small-to-medium experiment counts, want UI without running a server | `references/sqlite-local.md` |
50	| **Docker Compose stack** ⭐ | `http://host:8000` (PostgreSQL + MinIO) | Team use, production, parallel jobs, large artifacts, model registry across projects | `references/docker-compose-server.md` + `assets/docker-compose-stack/` |
51	| Databricks-managed | `databricks://` | Already paying for Databricks | (out of scope; defer to Databricks docs) |
52	
53	The two starred modes cover ~95% of real use. **Default**: SQLite for quick experiments, Docker Compose stack when more than one person needs to see the same runs.
54	
55	### File mode is for transient runs only
56	
57	The default `file:./mlruns` mode does NOT support the model registry — `mlflow.register_model()` raises. If the user wants a registry **at all**, they need SQLite or a server backend, even for solo use.
58	
59	## Workflow
60	
61	### 1. Initialize the chosen mode
62	
63	**SQLite (recommended for solo)**:
64	
65	```bash
66	bash skills/local/mlflow-tracking/scripts/init-mlflow-sqlite.sh
67	# Creates mlflow.db, .gitignore entries, prints the URL to launch `mlflow ui`
68	```
69	
70	**Docker Compose stack (recommended for team)**:
71	
72	```bash
73	bash skills/local/mlflow-tracking/scripts/start-mlflow-server.sh --target-dir infra/mlflow
74	# Copies assets/docker-compose-stack/ into infra/mlflow/, customizes .env,
75	# runs `docker compose up -d`, waits for the healthcheck, prints the URL.
76	```
77	
78	### 2. Set the tracking URI in your code
79	
80	```python
81	import mlflow
82	
83	# SQLite mode:
84	mlflow.set_tracking_uri("sqlite:///mlflow.db")
85	
86	# Server mode:
87	mlflow.set_tracking_uri("http://localhost:8000")
88	```
89	
90	Or via env var (preferred for subprocess / CI consistency):
91	
92	```bash
93	export MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=sqlite:///mlflow.db
94	# or
95	export MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://localhost:8000
96	```
97	
98	`set_tracking_uri()` only affects the current process. Subprocesses MUST use the env var.
99	
100	### 3. Log a run
101	
102	Two equally-valid styles. **Pick one**, don't mix in the same script.
103	
104	**Manual logging** (full control):
105	
106	```python
107	mlflow.set_experiment("my-project")           # creates if missing
108	
109	with mlflow.start_run(run_name="baseline"):
110	    mlflow.log_params({"lr": 1e-3, "epochs": 25})
111	    for epoch in range(25):
112	        loss = train_step()
113	        mlflow.log_metric("train_loss", loss, step=epoch)
114	    mlflow.log_artifact("config.yaml")
115	    mlflow.sklearn.log_model(model, "model")
116	```
117	
118	**Autologging** (zero-touch — preferred for supported frameworks):
119	
120	```python
121	import mlflow
122	mlflow.autolog()                              # detects framework at first .fit()
123	# OR explicit:
124	mlflow.sklearn.autolog()
125	mlflow.pytorch.autolog()
126	mlflow.transformers.autolog()
127	
128	with mlflow.start_run():
129	    model.fit(X, y)                           # params, metrics, model all logged
130	```
131	
132	For per-framework caveats and the full list of supported libraries, **read** `references/autologging-by-framework.md`.
133	
134	### 4. View results
135	
136	```bash
137	# SQLite mode — must pass the same URI explicitly:
138	mlflow ui --backend-store-uri sqlite:///mlflow.db --port 5001
139	
140	# Server mode — already has a UI at http://localhost:8000
141	```
142	
143	For programmatic access:
144	
145	```python
146	runs = mlflow.search_runs(experiment_names=["my-project"])    # pandas DataFrame
147	best = runs.sort_values("metrics.val_acc", ascending=False).iloc[0]
148	```
149	
150	The bundled `scripts/tail-runs.sh` wraps `mlflow.search_runs` for terminal use.
151	
152	### 5. Promote a model with the registry
153	
154	```python
155	mlflow.set_registry_uri(mlflow.get_tracking_uri())   # usually unnecessary; auto-inherits
156	
157	# Register from a logged run:
158	result = mlflow.register_model(
159	    f"runs:/{run_id}/model",
160	    name="my-model",
161	)
162	
163	# Set an alias (replaces deprecated stages):
164	client = mlflow.MlflowClient()
165	client.set_registered_model_alias("my-model", "Champion", version=result.version)
166	
167	# Load by alias:
168	model = mlflow.pyfunc.load_model("models:/my-model@Champion")
169	```
170	
171	For aliases vs deprecated stages, model versioning, and webhooks, **read** `references/model-registry.md`.
172	
173	### 6. (Optional) Trace LLM calls
174	
175	MLflow 2.14+ ships an OpenTelemetry-style tracing system that competes with W&B Weave / LangSmith / LangFuse:
176	
177	```python
178	import mlflow
179	mlflow.openai.autolog()         # auto-trace every OpenAI SDK call
180	# also: mlflow.anthropic / langchain / llama_index / dspy / autogen / crewai / litellm
181	
182	# Or manual spans:
183	@mlflow.trace
184	def my_chain(query):
185	    return rag(query)
186	```
187	
188	Traces show in the MLflow UI under the "Traces" tab. For provider matrix and trace querying, **read** `references/llm-tracing.md`.
189	
190	### 7. (Optional) Live charts in marimo / Jupyter
191	
192	Use `mlflow-widgets` (your own anywidget) for live-updating charts inside notebooks without spinning up the UI:
193	
194	```python
195	from mlflow_widgets import MlflowChart
196	MlflowChart(experiment_name="my-project", metric="val_loss")
197	```
198	
199	See `references/mlflow-widgets-anywidget.md` for installation and embedding patterns.
200	
201	## Available scripts
202	
203	- **`scripts/init-mlflow-sqlite.sh`** — Idempotent SQLite-mode init: touches `mlflow.db` if missing, adds `.gitignore` entries (`mlflow.db`, `mlruns/`, `mlartifacts/`), prints the exact `mlflow ui` command and `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` value to export.
204	  - Flags: `--db-path PATH` (default `mlflow.db`), `--port N` (default 5001), `--dry-run`, `--help`
205	- **`scripts/start-mlflow-server.sh`** — Copy `assets/docker-compose-stack/` into a target directory, generate `.env` from template (with secret rotation prompt), `docker compose up -d`, wait for healthcheck, print URLs.
206	  - Flags: `--target-dir DIR` (default `infra/mlflow`), `--port N` (default 8000), `--no-rotate-secrets`, `--dry-run`, `--help`
207	- **`scripts/tail-runs.sh`** — Wrap `mlflow.search_runs()` for terminal use. PEP 723 inline deps — runs via `uv run` with no setup. Outputs CSV/JSON to stdout.
208	  - Flags: `--experiment NAME`, `--top-n N`, `--sort-by METRIC`, `--format {json,csv}`, `--tracking-uri URI`, `--help`
209	
210	## Bundled assets
211	
212	- `assets/docker-compose-stack/` — Production-grade MLflow server: `docker-compose.yaml` (PostgreSQL + MinIO + tracking server + bucket bootstrap), `Dockerfile` (pinned MLflow image + psycopg2 + boto3), `.env.example`, `.gitignore`, `README.md`. Copy the whole folder into `<project>/infra/mlflow/`.

214	## Reference files
215	
216	- `references/sqlite-local.md` — Read **when** the user picks SQLite mode or asks about `mlflow ui` not finding their runs. Covers the explicit `--backend-store-uri` requirement (the #1 SQLite-mode confusion).
217	- `references/docker-compose-server.md` — Read **when** deploying the server stack: customizing `.env`, persisting `mlflow_data/`, securing MinIO, using AWS S3 instead of MinIO, fronting with nginx + auth.
218	- `references/llm-tracing.md` — Read **when** the user asks about LLM observability, traces, prompts, token costs, or any of: OpenAI / Anthropic / LangChain / LlamaIndex / DSPy / AutoGen / CrewAI / LiteLLM. Covers `mlflow.<provider>.autolog`, `@mlflow.trace`, span attributes, and trace search.
219	- `references/model-registry.md` — Read **when** the user wants to manage model versions, promote between environments, or asks about Champion/Challenger. Covers aliases (current API) vs stages (deprecated), `MlflowClient`, webhooks.
220	- `references/autologging-by-framework.md` — Read **when** picking autolog for a specific library. Covers all officially-supported frameworks (sklearn, pytorch, lightning, tensorflow, keras, xgboost, lightgbm, catboost, statsmodels, spark, fastai, gluon, paddle, transformers) with per-framework gotchas.
221	- `references/mlflow-widgets-anywidget.md` — Read **when** the user wants live charts inside marimo or Jupyter without launching the full MLflow UI. Covers installation, the `MlflowChart` API, and embedding patterns.
222	
223	## Gotchas
224	
225	- **`mlflow ui` does NOT auto-pick up `sqlite:///mlflow.db`.** It defaults to `./mlruns/`. You MUST pass `--backend-store-uri sqlite:///mlflow.db` (matching what your code uses) or you'll see an empty UI. The init script prints the right command.
226	- **`set_tracking_uri()` is process-local.** Subprocesses (e.g., `subprocess.run`, `joblib`, `multiprocessing`) won't inherit it unless you set `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` in the environment first.
227	- **Autolog must be called BEFORE `start_run()`** (or before the first `.fit()` if you're not using a context manager). Calling it after silently logs nothing.
228	- **Model registry requires a database backend**. `file:./mlruns` raises on `register_model`. SQLite, PostgreSQL, and MySQL all work.
229	- **macOS port 5000 conflict**: AirPlay Receiver hijacks port 5000. The Docker stack uses 8000; the SQLite UI script uses 5001. If the user insists on 5000, tell them to disable AirPlay Receiver in System Settings → General → AirDrop & Handoff.
230	- **`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` must be set in the CLIENT environment** when using a server with S3/MinIO artifacts — the MLflow client uploads artifacts directly to S3, not via the server. Server-side env vars are not enough.
231	- **SQLite + parallel workers = `database is locked`.** SQLite serializes writes. Once the user is running >1 trainer at a time, migrate to the Docker stack (PostgreSQL).
232	- **Stages (`Staging` / `Production`) are deprecated** in MLflow ≥ 2.9. Use **aliases** (`Champion`, `Challenger`, etc.). Old code with `transition_model_version_stage()` still works but emits warnings; new code should use `set_registered_model_alias()`.
233	- **Run names are NOT unique** within an experiment. Two runs can both be named `"baseline"`. Identity = `run_id` (UUID). Set explicit, semantic `run_name` for human readability, but use `run_id` programmatically.
234	- **`MLFLOW_REGISTRY_URI` is almost never needed.** When tracking URI is HTTP / SQLite / PostgreSQL, the registry uses the same backend automatically. Setting both to different values is an advanced setup; don't do it by default.
